questions.text: A landscape designer is preparing a site plan for a large residential development that includes a planned Material Recovery Facility (MRF) for waste segregation. Which law mandates the inclusion of this facility, and what is its primary function?

options.text: **RA 9275** requires MRFs to treat wastewater from residential units, ensuring compliance with environmental standards
**RA 9003** requires LGUs and residential projects to establish MRFs for waste segregation and recycling
**PD 1586** requires MRFs as part of environmental impact mitigation, focusing on reducing ecological footprints
MRFs are optional facilities not required by any Philippine law, though they are encouraged for sustainability

rationale.a: RA 9275 requires STPs for wastewater treatment, not MRFs. MRFs handle solid waste, not wastewater.
rationale.b: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act) mandates that LGUs establish MRFs and residential projects include waste management facilities. The MRF is where waste is sorted into recyclable and compostable materials, reducing disposal to landfills.
rationale.c: While PD 1586 requires environmental mitigation, MRF is specifically mandated by RA 9003.
rationale.d: RA 9003 makes MRFs mandatory for proper waste management and environmental protection.
rationale.correct: RA 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act) mandates that LGUs establish MRFs and residential projects include waste management facilities. The MRF is where waste is sorted into recyclable and compostable materials, reducing disposal to landfills.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9003 mandates MRFs as infrastructure for waste segregation and recycling in residential and LGU projects.

questions.text: A residential subdivision project is proposed on a 50-hectare site in a valley with several streams and no proximity to protected areas. The site is not in an Environmentally Critical Area. Which environmental legal requirement applies?

options.text: Full Environmental Impact Statement and ECC are mandatory because the site is large and may impact local ecosystems
No EIS or ECC is required because the site is not in an ECA, and the development is considered low-risk
PD 1067 easement requirements apply to identified streams; ECC may not be required if not in ECA
Only RA 9003 solid waste management requirements apply, focusing on waste reduction and recycling initiatives

rationale.a: Large size alone does not trigger ECC; ECP category or ECA location does.
rationale.b: Even outside ECAs, PD 1067 applies—water body easements are always required.
rationale.c: PD 1067 easements are mandatory regardless of ECA status. For projects not in ECAs but not in ECP categories, ECC may not be required. However, the site must comply with PD 1067 easement distances for all identified streams. Landscape design must reserve these easements and prevent building placement within them.
rationale.d: While RA 9003 applies, PD 1067 easements are the most relevant legal constraint for this site.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 easements are mandatory regardless of ECA status. For projects not in ECAs but not in ECP categories, ECC may not be required. However, the site must comply with PD 1067 easement distances for all identified streams. Landscape design must reserve these easements and prevent building placement within them.
rationale.takeaway: All sites with water bodies must comply with PD 1067; ECC requirements depend on ECP category or ECA location.

questions.text: A development site is adjacent to a NIPAS (National Integrated Protected Areas System) protected landscape. The developer proposes a residential project in the buffer zone of the protected area. Analyze what legal framework applies and what restrictions the designer should expect:

options.text: No restrictions apply because the project is not inside the protected area, only adjacent to it, which may be a common misconception
**RA 7586** applies; DENR permits are required; design must demonstrate that the project does not harm protected species or ecosystems
Only municipal zoning ordinances apply; NIPAS has no jurisdiction outside protected area boundaries, which limits its influence
**RA 9275** prohibits all development adjacent to protected areas, ensuring no environmental impact

rationale.a: Buffer zones around protected areas are subject to NIPAS restrictions; proximity matters.
rationale.b: RA 7586 NIPAS Act extends oversight to buffer zones around protected areas. Projects in or near NIPAS must obtain special permits from DENR. Design must incorporate conservation measures and demonstrate that development does not harm protected ecosystems or species.
rationale.c: NIPAS has authority over buffer zones and must approve development plans affecting protected area ecology.
rationale.d: RA 9275 (water quality) does not prohibit all development near protected areas; RA 7586 NIPAS does require permits and harm assessment.
rationale.correct: RA 7586 NIPAS Act extends oversight to buffer zones around protected areas. Projects in or near NIPAS must obtain special permits from DENR. Design must incorporate conservation measures and demonstrate that development does not harm protected ecosystems or species.
rationale.takeaway: NIPAS buffer zones require DENR permits and restrictions to protect adjacent protected areas from development impacts.

questions.text: According to **PD 1067** (Water Code of the Philippines), what is the required easement distance from the edge of a river that is 5 meters wide?

options.text: 3 meters
10 meters
20 meters
40 meters

rationale.a: PD 1067 establishes 3-meter easement for streams and rivers less than 6 meters wide. Since this river is 5 meters wide (< 6m), the easement is 3 meters.
rationale.b: 10 meters is not a PD 1067 easement distance.
rationale.c: 20 meters applies to rivers 6 meters wide or greater.
rationale.d: 40 meters applies to lakes and seashore.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 Article 51 requires easement of 3m (urban land), 20m (agricultural land), or 40m (forest land) along rivers, measured from highest water line. Land classification required to determine distance.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easement distances vary by water body size: 3m (< 6m width), 20m (≥ 6m), 40m (lakes/sea).

questions.text: A proposed development project is located in a mangrove ecosystem. Which Philippine law requires the project to undergo environmental impact assessment and obtain a compliance certificate?

options.text: **PD 957** (Subdivision and Condominium Buyers Protective Decree)
**RA 7279** (Urban Development and Housing Act)
**PD 1586** (Philippine Environmental Impact Statement System)
**RA 9003** (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act)

rationale.a: PD 957 governs subdivision buyer protection and developer registration, not environmental assessment.
rationale.b: RA 7279 addresses housing eviction and relocation, not environmental assessment.
rationale.c: Mangrove ecosystems are designated Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) under PD 1586. Projects in ECAs must undergo EIA and obtain ECC. Mangrove areas are explicitly listed as sensitive ecosystems requiring assessment.
rationale.d: RA 9003 governs solid waste management, not environmental impact for development in sensitive ecosystems.
rationale.correct: Mangrove ecosystems are designated Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA) under PD 1586. Projects in ECAs must undergo EIA and obtain ECC. Mangrove areas are explicitly listed as sensitive ecosystems requiring assessment.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1586 requires environmental assessment for projects in Environmentally Critical Areas, including mangroves.

questions.text: Which agency is responsible for issuing an **ECC (Environmental Compliance Certificate)** under **PD 1586**?

options.text: DHSUD (Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development)
DENR (Department of Environment and Natural Resources)
DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways)
Local Government Unit (LGU) planning office

rationale.a: DHSUD regulates subdivisions and housing projects but does not issue ECC. [ERR-PLAN-021]
rationale.b: PD 1586 establishes the EIS system and designates DENR as the issuing agency for ECC. DENR conducts the environmental impact assessment for Environmentally Critical Projects and issues the ECC.
rationale.c: DPWH is responsible for public infrastructure but not ECC issuance.
rationale.d: LGUs coordinate with DENR but do not issue the ECC.
rationale.correct: PD 1586 establishes the EIS system and designates DENR as the issuing agency for ECC. DENR conducts the environmental impact assessment for Environmentally Critical Projects and issues the ECC.
rationale.takeaway: DENR issues ECC under PD 1586; DHSUD handles subdivision permits (distinct agencies, distinct roles).

questions.text: A landscape architect discovers that a proposed site is in an area with unclear ECA status and proximity to an estero of unknown width. The client pressures to proceed without environmental assessment. Analyze what legal and professional responsibilities apply:

options.text: Proceed immediately to design; environmental assessment can be done later if required, assuming no immediate legal constraints
Verify estero width and ECA status with DENR before design; verify PD 1067 easement distance; determine if ECC is required
Assume no environmental requirements apply because the site is developed area, thus bypassing initial assessments
Environmental assessment is only required for projects in protected areas, not for developed or urban sites

rationale.a: Proceeding without environmental assessment risks legal liability and project redesign costs.
rationale.b: Professional practice requires due diligence: verify water body dimensions (to apply correct PD 1067 easement), confirm ECA status with DENR (to determine EIS requirement), and confirm whether project is classified as ECP requiring ECC. Design cannot responsibly proceed without clarifying these legal constraints.
rationale.c: Even developed areas must comply with PD 1067; ECA status depends on specific site characteristics, not general area designation.
rationale.d: ECC requirements apply to ECPs and ECA projects, not only protected areas.
rationale.correct: Professional practice requires due diligence: verify water body dimensions (to apply correct PD 1067 easement), confirm ECA status with DENR (to determine EIS requirement), and confirm whether project is classified as ECP requiring ECC. Design cannot responsibly proceed without clarifying these legal constraints.
rationale.takeaway: Environmental due diligence is essential before site design to identify legal requirements and avoid costly non-compliance.

questions.text: A site plan for a mixed-use development includes a large lake, steep riparian forest, and commercial buildings. Integrate **PD 1067**, **PD 1586**, **RA 7586**, **RA 9275**, and **RA 9003** requirements into a design checklist. Which combination of measures demonstrates full legal compliance?

options.text: Reserve easement from lake edge per PD 1067 Article 51: 3m (urban land), 20m (agricultural land), or 40m (forest land), assess if EIA required in forest (PD 1586), include STP (RA 9275) and MRF (RA 9003)
Maximize lake-side development to generate views; no STP required for small commercial use, assuming minimal environmental impact
Reserve forest as protected area; prohibit all development; no wastewater or waste management needed, as natural processes will suffice
Environmental compliance applies only to public projects, not private developments, allowing for more flexible design approaches

rationale.a: Comprehensive compliance requires: (1) 40m easement from lake (PD 1067); (2) EIA assessment if forest is in ECA or project is ECP (PD 1586); (3) STP for commercial wastewater (RA 9275); (4) MRF for solid waste management (RA 9003). RA 7586 may apply if near protected area. All integrate into site planning.
rationale.b: Lake-side development cannot violate PD 1067 easement; STP is mandatory for commercial buildings under RA 9275.
rationale.c: Riparian forest protection is important but does not eliminate other compliance requirements (STP, MRF).
rationale.d: Environmental laws apply to all development, public and private.
rationale.correct: Comprehensive compliance requires: (1) 40m easement from lake (PD 1067); (2) EIA assessment if forest is in ECA or project is ECP (PD 1586); (3) STP for commercial wastewater (RA 9275); (4) MRF for solid waste management (RA 9003). RA 7586 may apply if near protected area. All integrate into site planning.
rationale.takeaway: Comprehensive environmental site planning integrates multiple laws: water easements, EIS, protected areas, wastewater, waste management.

questions.text: A landscape site plan identifies an estero (drainage canal, 4 meters wide) running along the site boundary. According to **PD 1067**, what area must be reserved as public right-of-way and cannot be developed?

options.text: 3 meters from the estero edge (because width < 6 meters)
20 meters from the estero edge, which is a standard buffer zone for larger waterways
The entire site within 100 meters of the estero, which is a precautionary measure for flood-prone areas
No easement required for drainage canals, unless specified by local ordinances

rationale.a: PD 1067 requires 3-meter easement from streams and rivers less than 6 meters wide. A 4-meter-wide estero is less than 6 meters, so 3 meters of right-of-way must be reserved along the estero edge.
rationale.b: 20 meters applies to rivers 6 meters wide or greater, not to this 4-meter estero.
rationale.c: Only the 3-meter strip is reserved; the remainder of the site may be developed.
rationale.d: Drainage canals and esteros are water bodies subject to easement requirements.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 requires 3-meter easement from streams and rivers less than 6 meters wide. A 4-meter-wide estero is less than 6 meters, so 3 meters of right-of-way must be reserved along the estero edge.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easement for esteros < 6m wide = 3 meters; this area is public right-of-way.

questions.text: **RA 9275** (Philippine Clean Water Act) requires high-density residential developments to include what infrastructure to prevent water pollution?

options.text: Open stormwater drainage channels, which are designed to manage surface runoff
Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) or connection to municipal treatment
Groundwater extraction wells, which are used to supplement water supply
Drinking water filtration systems for residents, ensuring potable water quality

rationale.a: Stormwater drainage is distinct from sewage treatment; drainage alone does not treat wastewater.
rationale.b: RA 9275 requires sewage treatment to prevent raw wastewater discharge into water bodies. High-density residential and commercial projects must install and operate STPs or connect to municipal sewage systems with treatment.
rationale.c: Groundwater extraction is water supply, not wastewater treatment.
rationale.d: Drinking water filtration is for potable water, not treatment of wastewater before discharge.
rationale.correct: RA 9275 requires sewage treatment to prevent raw wastewater discharge into water bodies. High-density residential and commercial projects must install and operate STPs or connect to municipal sewage systems with treatment.
rationale.takeaway: RA 9275 mandates sewage treatment (STP) for high-density residential and commercial projects to protect water bodies.
